basics.name: Ibrahim Said Ahmad
basics.label: Assistant Professor, University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point
basics.summary: Computer scientist and NLP researcher specializing in natural language processing for low-resource languages, computational social science, and cross-cultural AI. Co-founder of HausaNLP and Arewa Data Science, with 10+ years of experience in teaching, research, and interdisciplinary collaboration across Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas. Published 40+ peer-reviewed papers, several recognized with best paper and best resource paper awards, and secured over $800,000 in competitive research grants.

work.name: University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point
work.position: Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and New Media Technologies
work.summary: Teaching, mentoring, and research in emotion-aware, culturally-informed AI.
highlights: Co-leading WARAKA, an open annotation platform and playbook for African-language datasets, as Co-PI on the Masakhane African Languages Hub grant.
Co-developed POLAR, a 23,000+ instance benchmark for multilingual, multicultural online polarization detection, and co-organized the SemEval-2026 shared task built on it.
Contributed to PLACES, a participatory red-teaming study and dataset for text-to-image safety in the Global South, published at FAccT 2026.

work.name: Northeastern University
work.position: Postdoctoral Research Fellow, Institute for Experiential AI
work.summary: Research at the intersection of NLP and computational social science, focused on low-resource languages and cross-cultural AI.
highlights: Co-developed BRIGHTER, a human-annotated emotion dataset for 28 languages (18 African); published at ACL 2025 (Best Resource Paper Award) with a companion SemEval 2025 shared task (Best Task Paper Award).
Developed AfriHate, the first labelled hate speech dataset for 18 African languages from 6 countries.
Studied cross-cultural emotion representation in LLMs; published at ACII 2024 (Best Paper Award).

work.name: Bayero University Kano
work.summary: Taught and researched AI, machine learning, and database systems; mentored graduate students.
highlights: Developed NaijaSenti, the first large-scale annotated Twitter sentiment corpus for the four main Nigerian languages.
Built and annotated a Twitter dataset on COVID-19 vaccination sentiment in Nigerian cyberspace.

work.name: Bayero University Kano
work.summary: Promoted to Lecturer II in 2017 while on PhD study fellowship.
